pairing.name: Friendly
pairing.mood: Soft and approachable without being childish. A warm, chunky serif headline with a round, modern sans.

display.notes: Single weight; inspired by Plantin Infant and ITC Italian Old Style.

body.notes: Made for Moldova; on Google Fonts since 2023.

hand.mood: A quick ballpoint note, narrow and fluent. Fits margins and small spaces.
hand.useFor: Margin notes, arrows with a word, 'from us' sign-offs, scrapbook notes.
hand.avoidFor: Small sizes: its x-height is low, so it shrinks faster than it looks.

tierRules.label: Glance
tierRules.summary: Quick pen or marker. A few words that are read in one look.
roles: price tag (word only, not the number)

style.$comment: Handwritten accent faces from foundations/typography/source/handwritten.json. use: none | accent (one short element) | core (part of the style). A product picks one in brand.json -> typography.hand.
style.why: The hand mainly lives in the ink line. One short note in a plain pen hand can add a person to warm pieces (Schroll et al. 2018), as long as the headline and body stay in the pairing.

rules: Two families at most (display + body), plus a mono for small data such as dates, prices and codes.
Sentence case everywhere. All capitals only for short labels of one to three words, with letter-spacing.
Three sizes per piece is usually enough: headline, body, small.
Big headlines get tight leading (about 1.0) and slightly negative tracking; body text gets 1.5 leading and lines of 45-75 characters.
Left-align text. Centre only one or two short lines on a centred poster.
Handwriting fonts only as one short accent, from source/handwritten.json, where the style allows it (approaches/<id>/typography.json -> handwritten). Never for body, prices, data, steps or buttons.
Match headline weight to the illustration: the stems of headline letters should be about as thick as the ink line.
